subject: Live status page: notice of sustained throughput variance affecting hosted inference
messages:

Subject: Live status page: temporary throughput variance impacting hosted inference (US region)

Hi Kira —

We wanted to alert you that we’ve posted a status update on our public status page: a sustained increase in p95 generation latency and reduced request throughput in our US host pool that may affect some in-flight requests for Crestmont Health. Our monitoring detected the signal ~08:45 PST; we opened an incident and have engineers actively investigating.

What you may see: elevated p95 and occasional 503s for short windows, primarily on long-sequence generation workloads. We have not detected data integrity issues.

Immediate actions in flight:
- Router-level throttles applied to reduce fanout on the affected pool.
- Autoscaler paused temporarily to avoid noisy scaling events while we triage.
- Engineers are gathering tracer IDs and sample request IDs; please share any sample request IDs you’ve seen with elevated latency.

We’ll send a 30-minute update and post the progress to the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-27-throughput-variance

Apologies for the interruption — I’ll keep you posted.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Incident 2026-11-27 — initial triage notes

Quick triage notes:
- Tokenized request distribution shows a spike of long-sequence jobs from a small subset of customers starting ~08:30 PST (matching Kira’s timing).
- Autoscaler backpressure + router fanout combined to create request queuing on the affected GPU pool; KV cache churn observed.
- No underlying host hardware faults; all GPU health checks passing.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Reduced max-concurrent per-tenant on the pool (soft throttle) — buys headroom.
2) Pinned small fraction of traffic to a warm spare pool to reduce tail latency while we evaluate cache policies.

I’ve uploaded a CSV timeline and a p95 trend chart to the incident folder. Will follow with logs for the sample request IDs Kira provided.

—Sean
SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-27T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: Final update: incident mitigated; next steps and post-incident follow-up

Hi Kira — following up with the final update for today’s incident.

Summary: Between ~08:30–11:10 PST we observed elevated p95 and intermittent 503s in the US hosted pool driven by an unexpected concentration of long-sequence requests and KV cache churn that increased tail latency under sustained load.

What we changed:
- Tuned router fanout and reduced per-tenant concurrency limits during the window.
- Migrated a small fraction of traffic to a warm spare pool while cache pressure stabilized.
- Rebalanced KV cache eviction thresholds to reduce churn for long-sequence workloads.

Impact: Customers may have experienced higher p95 and a small number of timeouts (we saw ~0.6% of requests return 503 during peak). We logged the sample request IDs Kira provided; those were included in the analysis.

Current status: The US pool is stable and within normal SLO bounds. We have reverted the temporary throttles and will continue to monitor.

Follow-up items (we’ll share a short post-incident note next week):
1) Deeper cache-coherence analysis to understand eviction sensitivity to long-sequence patterns.
2) Improve per-tenant traffic shaping recommendations for customers with bursty long-sequence usage.
3) Consider a default warm-pool reserve for customers with sustained long-seq footprints.

Post-incident doc and timeline: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-incident-data
Public status page event: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-27-throughput-variance

If you want a scheduled review of the logs and traces, we can set that up for next week — happy to coordinate dates.

Thanks for your patience; we’ll follow up with the written RCA and recommended mitigations.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
